newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenia to sell off communications, cognac plant.
newsitem.headline: Armenia to sell off communications, cognac plant.

text.p: Armenia will privatise two major enterprises -- the Armentel communications joint-venture and the Yerevan Cognac Plant -- and 11 smaller enterprises through open tenders, the Economy Minister said on Monday.
"We are going to sell the 51 percent state-owned stake of the main telephone company of Armenia," Vakhram Avanesyan told a news conference.
He did not mention the estimated value of the enterprises, explaining this could put off investors.
"It is a very complicated question and we should not scare our customers," he said.

Avanesyan said U.S. company Transworld Telecommunications Inc, which owns 49 percent of Armentel, would sell its stake as well. Armentel JV handles international communications in the former Soviet republic of 3.5 million people.
Armentel is being offered at a tender for strategic investors, and the winning bid will be the one with the highest offer price, he said. The deadline for submitting bids is October 1.
Avanesyan said 80 percent of shares in the Yerevan Cognac Plant would be sold off. "The rest will remain in the hands of plant employees," he said.

The cognac plant and another 11 enterprises will be offered at an investment tender, and the authorities will take into account not only the offer price but also investment plans and employment guarantees in awarding the stakes, he said.
The new owners of the cognac producer will be obliged to use only domestically produced raw materials.

The Yerevan plant is legendary throughout the former Soviet union for the wide array of cognacs it produces, revered by Kremlin leaders from Stalin to Mikhail Gorbachev. Winston Churchill was known to have been partial to it too.

The plant, which has the capacity to produce up 1.5 million decaliters per year, put out just 253,000 decaliters in 1996. Most of that was exported to Russia. By the end of 1996 the plant had run up tax arrears of $1.9 million.
The deadline for bids is October 15, he said.
Merrill Lynch International is acting as adviser to the government on the sales, he said.
